neet_che_u02_t12_1.working: A half-filled 3d subshell is extra stable, so one 4s electron moves to 3d. This gives [Ar] 3d5 4s1.

neet_che_u02_t12_2.working: N3- (7+3), O2- (8+2), F- (9+1) and Na+ (11-1) each have 10 electrons. Every other set includes a species with 18 electrons (Cl-, S2-, K+).

neet_che_u02_t12_3.working: Fe is [Ar] 3d6 4s2. The two 4s electrons are removed first, leaving [Ar] 3d6.

neet_che_u02_t12_4.working: A is true: for K, 4s is lower in energy than 3d (n+l rule), so 4s fills first. R is true: cations lose 4s electrons before 3d. However, R is about ionisation of transition-metal cations, not the filling order in K, so it does not explain A.

neet_che_u02_t12_5.working: Statement I is wrong: Mn is [Ar] 3d5 4s2, so Mn2+ is [Ar] 3d5. Statement II is wrong: unpaired electrons are Cr 6 (3d5 4s1), Mn 5, Fe 4, Cu 1, so Cr has the most.
